claims.claim: In late October, HHS said it does not intend to take enforcement action against state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities, or licensed physicians compounding six unapproved peptides.
claims.episode_span: the US Department of Health and Human Services said it does not intend to take enforcement action
claims.source_title: HHS greenlights sale of six unapproved peptides despite FDA guidance
claims.supporting_quote: The US Department of Health and Human Services said in late October that it does not intend to take enforcement action against state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities, or licensed physicians who compound six peptide substances the Food and Drug Administration has not approved.

claims.claim: The six peptides are BPC-157, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, semax and TB-500, recommended for compounding by an FDA advisory committee in July.
claims.episode_span: The six are BPC-157, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, semax and TB-500
claims.source_title: HHS greenlights sale of six unapproved peptides despite FDA guidance
claims.supporting_quote: The six are BPC-157, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, semax and TB-500, the same set an FDA advisory committee recommended for compounding in July.

claims.claim: The enforcement policy does not approve the drugs or find them safe or effective, and it asks for preliminary identity and quality standards.
claims.episode_span: The enforcement policy does not approve the drugs or find them safe or effective.
claims.source_title: HHS greenlights sale of six unapproved peptides despite FDA guidance
claims.supporting_quote: The enforcement policy does not approve the drugs or find them safe or effective. It does ask for preliminary identity and quality standards, and officials describe the aim as moving patients away from research-use-only products sold online.

claims.claim: The policy was announced on October 28, 2026, and signed by Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

claims.claim: Lee Rosebush supported the decision as a move away from gray and black markets, and Fred Mills warned against treating consumers as test subjects.

claims.claim: Among 10,878 new oral semaglutide users with type 2 diabetes and ASCVD, risks of 3-point and modified 3-point MACE were 17 percent and 21 percent lower than among 28,639 users of other noninsulin glucose-lowering therapies.
claims.episode_span: a 17 percent lower risk of 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events and a 21 percent lower risk
claims.source_title: Comparing Cardiovascular Outcomes in New Users of Oral Semaglutide Versus Other Noninsulin Glucose-Lowering Therapies
claims.supporting_quote: Oral semaglutide users (n = 10,878) had risk reductions of 17% and 21% in 3- and modified 3-point MACE, respectively, and significant risk reductions in 5-, modified 5-, and 2-point MACE, IS, and all-cause death vs ONIGLT users (n = 28,639).

claims.claim: Matched comparisons showed 22 percent and 24 percent lower 3-point and modified 3-point MACE risks versus DPP-4 inhibitors, and 21 percent and 22 percent lower risks versus SGLT2 inhibitors.
